answer:
A gated FFN computes down(activation(gate(x)) ⊙ up(x)). SwiGLU uses SiLU, while GeGLU uses GELU. Fusing gate/up projections keeps the code simple and performs one larger input matmul. There are three weight matrices; an intermediate width near 8D/3 matches the parameter count of a conventional two-matrix FFN with width 4D, ignoring rounding and biases.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** SwiGLU uses $y=W_d[\operatorname{SiLU}(W_gx)\odot(W_ux)]$, with $\operatorname{SiLU}(z)=z\sigma(z)$. Ignoring biases, its parameter count is $3Dd_{ff}$ rather than $2Dd_{ff}$. Matching a conventional width-$4D$ FFN therefore suggests $d_{ff}\approx8D/3$, before hardware-friendly rounding. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.05202)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://azizbelaweid.substack.com/p/what-is-swiglu-how-to-implement-it) and [2](https://theorempath.com/compare/swiglu-vs-gelu-vs-relu).
